test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting second to the left of T. Only two people are sitting between S and R. M is not the immediate neighbour of S. P is sitting second to the right of R.

How many people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N?
solution:
Given: T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) S is sitting second to the left of T. 

2) Only two people are sitting between S and R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292c2479e5ba63fce7fe738fcaa70b14f137471275597173b2a0cf10f3241408.png] 

3) M is not the immediate neighbour of S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3736359cbc5004f52310fe8f458b78f5d72661305a4aa03ee517165dd305e0ae.png] 

4) P is sitting second to the right of R.

After positioning P only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb552d8fb5b91536b6ed3788a5b66122c36be864ad8e46a7df800f3c50c8cd33.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement, two people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
